title: Unit circle & CAST
examples: How do I remember which trig functions are positive in each quadrant?
If I have an angle like three sixty minus theta, how do I solve it?
Can you show me an example of finding solutions for cosine using related angles?

explain.say: Today we explore the unit circle and finding solutions using quadrants.
The unit circle helps us find the values of sine and cosine for any angle.
We use the signs of the coordinates to know which trig functions are positive.
In the first quadrant, all trigonometric functions are positive there.
In the second quadrant, only sine and cosecant are positive values.

faq.q: How do I remember which functions are positive in each quadrant?
faq.a: A helpful way is to remember the acronym ASTC. A stands for all in the first quadrant. S for sine in the second quadrant.
asks: What does ASTC mean for trig signs?
Which quadrant has only sine positive?

faq.q: What is the relationship between an angle and its reference angle?
faq.a: The reference angle is the smallest acute angle the terminal side makes with the x-axis. It helps you find the basic value.
asks: How do I find the reference angle?
What is the reference angle for an angle in the third quadrant?

faq.q: When I use a related angle, do I change the sign of the function?
faq.a: You must check the quadrant of the original angle to determine the correct sign. The reference angle only gives the magnitude.
asks: Do I always use positive values for related angles?
How do I know if the result should be negative?

faq.q: Does the unit circle only work for degrees or radians?
faq.a: The unit circle works for both degrees and radians. Just make sure your calculator is set to the correct unit.
asks: Can I use radians on the unit circle?
What is the unit circle in degrees?

faq.q: If I find a solution in one quadrant, do I find solutions in others too?
faq.a: Yes, because trig functions are periodic, you find all solutions by adding multiples of the period. For sine and cosine, this is two pi.
asks: How do I find all possible answers?
What is the period for sine and cosine?

facts: The unit circle is a circle with a radius of one unit.
The coordinates (x, y) on the unit circle represent (cos(theta), sin(theta)).
The reference angle is always positive and acute, between zero and pi/2 radians.
The period of sine and cosine functions is two pi radians.

quiz.say: If an angle is in the second quadrant, what sign must the sine function have?
quiz.why: In the second quadrant, the x-coordinate is negative and the y-coordinate is positive, so sine must be positive.

wrong.1: This is tempting because the x-coordinate is negative, but sine corresponds to the y-coordinate.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because the angle is not on an axis, so the value cannot be zero.
wrong.3: This is too vague; the quadrant specifies the required sign for the function.

quiz.say: What is the reference angle for an angle of two three pi over four?
quiz.why: The angle two three pi over four is in the second quadrant, and its reference angle is pi minus two three pi over four, which equals pi/4.

wrong.0: This is the angle on the y-axis, not the specific reference angle for two three pi over four.
wrong.2: This is the actual angle, not the smallest acute reference angle.
wrong.3: This is the angle itself, not the reference angle relative to the x-axis.

quiz.say: If cos(theta) = negative one over two, and theta is in the third quadrant, what is the smallest positive solution for theta?
quiz.why: The reference angle for cosine being one over two is pi/3. In the third quadrant, we add pi to the reference angle: pi plus pi/3 equals four pi over three.

wrong.0: This angle is in the second quadrant, where cosine is negative, but the reference angle calculation is wrong for the third quadrant.
wrong.1: This is the reference angle, but the question asks for the actual angle in the third quadrant.
wrong.2: This is the angle on the negative x-axis, not the specific solution required.
